name: Roosevelt

{"pain_severity": <integer 0-10, your assessment of the patient's true pain>,
  "offer": "yes" or "no",
  "dose": "low", "high", or "none" (use "none" if you would not offer it),
  "explanation": <one sentence>}

Case: Roosevelt is a 62-year-old with history of lung cancer who presents with sudden onset of back pain. Roosevelt states that the pain began suddenly while he was cooking breakfast. Roosevelt asserts that the pain is worst in his lower back and radiates down the front of his thighs. Roosevelt has tried taking some ibuprofen and acetaminophen, but he has had no relief. On physical exam, you find that he is tender to palpation of the mid-lumbar spine and that he has pain limited-movement of his hip flexors. MRI of the lumbar spine reveals a pathologic fracture of his L3 vertebral body, canal and neuroforaminal stenosis, and evidence of metastatic disease.
